_about: What's new: shown from the version line under the main menu (src/menu/whatsNew.ts). Newest first. Keep entries short and player-friendly.

entries.title: Version 0.5.1: easier to read
entries.text: Rocks, shields and portals now show exactly what they do: rocks are drawn as their true bouncing edge, shields show where they face and how much they can take, and a portal's whole disc is its mouth.

entries.title: Portal discs and exit beams
entries.text: A shot that touches any part of a portal's disc now falls in. The old rim arrow is gone: a faint beam and chevrons show where shots come out. Shoot straight into one beam and the shot leaves the twin along its beam; at an angle, it leaves at that angle.

entries.title: Clearer shields
entries.text: A shield's barrier is drawn at its full blocking width with a dark edge, a faint chevron shows which way it faces (brighter when you hover or select it), and it has its own small health bar. The bar under the cannon is bigger and notched per hit.

entries.title: Rocks show their true edge
entries.text: A rock now fills exactly the oval that shots bounce off, with a dark outline on that edge and all its stone, cracks and moss inside it. No more shots seeming to hit thin air or slip into a bump.

entries.title: Version 0.5.0: bricks, portals and oval rocks
entries.text: Three more ways to play the angles: oval rock pillars, brick walls you can shoot down, and portals that send shots across the board. The AI knows them all. Try them on the new Warp Works map, or build your own in the editor.

entries.title: Portals
entries.text: A shot that falls into a portal comes out of its twin (same colour and mark) at the same speed, turned by the difference in their facings. No free range: the distance carries on. Aim lines show the way out. Editor: key 9 places a pair, Q/E turns a mouth.

entries.title: New map: Warp Works
entries.text: A fair, mirrored map with brick walls guarding the middle and two portal pairs that jump shots from low on your side to high on theirs. Play it vs AI or online, or open it in the editor from Map → Examples.

entries.title: Breakable walls
entries.text: Brick walls that bounce shots but wear down with every hit, from either side. They crack, then crumble for good, opening a new lane; the AI shoots them down when they hide its targets. In the editor, set a wall's Type to Breakable and pick its HP.

entries.title: Oval rock pillars
entries.text: Pillars are now drawn as rocks, so they never look like a cannon, and they can be ovals. In the editor, pick a preset (Small, Medium, Large, Oval, Long), set the width and height, and turn ovals with Q/E. Shots bounce off the true curve.

entries.title: Version 0.4.0: new obstacles
entries.text: Three new things to aim around: void walls that swallow shots, round pillars that bounce them off their curve, and one-way glass. The AI knows them too: it banks off pillars and glass and never wastes shots into the void.

entries.title: Void walls
entries.text: Dark purple walls with a slow swirl. Any shot that touches one vanishes in a puff, with no bounce, so they close off a lane completely.

entries.title: Round pillars
entries.text: Shots glance off a pillar like a ball off a post: hit it off-centre and the shot flies off at a wide angle. Handy for banking round a crowd.

entries.title: One-way glass
entries.text: Shots pass through a glass pane the way its arrows point and bounce off its bright side. Guard a cannon from one side while still firing out through it.

entries.title: Two new maps: Glass Garden and Void Gate
entries.text: Try the new obstacles in Play vs AI or online on two fair, mirrored maps. In the editor, Map → Examples opens a copy of either, and keys 6, 7 and 8 place void walls, pillars and glass (Q/E turns glass, F flips it).

entries.title: Bank shots keep their range
entries.text: A shot now flies a set distance, measured along its path, so banking off walls no longer cuts it short (it used to vanish on its 4th bounce). Snipers keep twice the range, and wind that slows a shot doesn't shorten it.

entries.title: Version 0.3.0: battles that pop
entries.text: Cannons glow in their team's colour and every shot leaves a trail. Muzzle flashes, smoke and recoil when they fire, sparks where shots hit or bank, barriers that shimmer and shatter, heal sparkles, and a burst when a cannon changes hands.

entries.title: Effects quality setting
entries.text: Settings → Display → Effects quality: High, Low or Off. It starts on High, or on Low on a slower device or if battles run slowly. Reduce motion stills the shakes and moving effects but keeps the glows.

entries.title: Version 0.2.6: pulse to the music
entries.text: While music plays, a few small things keep time with it: the jukebox bars bounce on each beat, and the title, Play button and board glow swell gently on each bar. In battle, just a faint shine on the top bar. Each song's beat was measured from its audio.

entries.title: Pulse to the music setting
entries.text: Settings → Music → Pulse to the music turns it off. It also stops when music is paused, muted or at volume 0, and with Reduce motion on.

entries.title: Version 0.2.5: a livelier feel
entries.text: Small touches all over: buttons lift and glow under the mouse and squish when pressed, pages and panels ease in, the result panel pops in with a few bits of confetti on a win, and the top bar shines when a cannon changes hands.

entries.title: Reduce motion setting
entries.text: Settings → Display → Reduce motion stills all of that movement. Auto, the default, follows your device’s own reduce-motion setting.

entries.title: Version 0.2.4: result buttons fit
entries.text: The buttons on the win, loss and surrender panel always fit their words now, sit side by side at the same size, and stack neatly on phones. On small screens the top bar tucks extra buttons into the Menu instead of cutting them off.

entries.title: Version 0.2.3: tidier Settings
entries.text: Every setting now sits on one compact row. The longer explanations moved behind a small ? next to each name: hover it, focus it, or tap it on a phone. The in-battle Settings panel is now readable on phones too.

entries.title: Version 0.2.2: smoother online play
entries.text: Online over long distances feels much smoother: your aims, tower swaps and auto toggles show the moment you click, and the board no longer freezes and jumps when the connection hiccups. Your ping now shows in the top bar.

entries.title: Pick where an online room runs
entries.text: When you create a room you can choose the server region, so a friend far away doesn’t carry all the delay. The lobby shows where the room landed and your ping.

entries.title: Version 0.2.1: switching away is safe
entries.text: Coming back to the tab no longer sets off a burst of sounds, and the You win / You lose panel always shows, even if the round ended while you were away.

entries.title: When tabbed out settings
entries.text: Two new switches in Settings: keep the music playing while you’re in another tab (on by default), and choose whether a round against the AI pauses or keeps going while you’re away.

entries.title: Version 0.2.0: the jukebox
entries.text: Music! Three songs by Reganati play from the menu straight into your battles and loop. Open the Jukebox (top left) to switch songs, star the one the game starts with, and set the music volume, apart from sound effects.

entries.title: A tidier main menu
entries.text: Profile moved to the top-right corner and the Jukebox sits top left, so the middle of the menu is lighter. Music is also in Settings and in the Menu during a battle.

entries.title: Profile, Credits and What’s new
entries.text: Your online name, skin, colour and difficulty live together in Profile, with a button to reset them. Credits has its own page. Tap the version under the menu to see this list, and use Copy debug info when you report a bug.

entries.title: The title battle stays after alt-tab
entries.text: The battle behind the main menu no longer disappears when you switch away and come back. Online, coming back jumps straight to the live round without a burst of old sounds.

entries.title: Battle top bar and Surrender
entries.text: Proper buttons that stay readable on phones and in Discord, a tug-of-war bar showing how many cannons each side holds, and Surrender (after a confirm) in every mode.

entries.title: Room settings and side glow
entries.text: Online hosts can pick the countdown (0, 3 or 5 s), turn pauses off and swap sides. Each half of the board glows softly in its team’s colour.

entries.title: Name tags when looks clash
entries.text: Online, everyone keeps their own skin and colour. If the two teams look too alike, small name tags appear on the cannons.

entries.title: Team colours
entries.text: Pick one of eight team colours. The AI always wears the colour that contrasts most with yours.

entries.title: 3-2-1-Go countdown
entries.text: Every round starts with a short countdown. You can already aim during it, and nobody fires before Go.

entries.title: Healers re-aim by themselves
entries.text: When a heal is done and auto-target is on, the healer picks a fresh target instead of waiting.

entries.title: Cannon skins
entries.text: Choose the shape of your cannons. A captured cannon takes its new owner’s skin.

entries.title: Heal guide
entries.text: How to play has a new card on healing your own cannons while they are being captured.

entries.title: Ownership rings
entries.text: A light ring marks your cannons and a red ring the enemy’s, so you can tell who owns what at a glance, whatever the colours.

entries.title: Difficulty retune
entries.text: Easy, Normal and Hard now land about 25%, 50% and 75% of first shots, and need a moment to correct after a miss. Impossible is unchanged.

entries.title: Back to editor
entries.text: When you test a map, a Back to editor button (or the E key) takes you straight back to your edit.

entries.title: Shield turns faster
entries.text: The Shield tower now turns three times as fast as a normal cannon, the quickest of all.
